name: ArchiMate 3.2
source: The Open Group ArchiMate 3.2 Specification: element types (ch. 4-13), relationship notation (ch. 5), relationship table (Appendix B, as encoded by the Archi project), basic viewpoints (Appendix C).

Organization.purpose: Structure of the enterprise: actors, roles, collaborations, their interfaces and locations.

Application Structure.purpose: Structure of one or more applications: components, interfaces and the data they use.

Information Structure.purpose: Information used in the enterprise and how it is represented.

Technology.purpose: Software and hardware that make up the technology layer.

Physical.purpose: Physical environment: equipment, facilities, distribution networks and materials.

Product.purpose: Value a product offers: its services, contracts and the parties involved.

Application Usage.purpose: How applications support business processes and actors.

Technology Usage.purpose: How applications are supported by technology.

Business Process Cooperation.purpose: Relationships between business processes and with their environment.

Application Cooperation.purpose: Relationships between applications: information flows and services.

Service Realization.purpose: How services are realized by behaviour and the elements assigned to it.

Implementation and Deployment.purpose: How applications are deployed on technology.

Stakeholder.purpose: Stakeholders, their drivers, assessments and the goals that address them.

Goal Realization.purpose: How goals are refined into outcomes, principles and requirements.

Requirements Realization.purpose: How requirements are realized by core elements.

Strategy.purpose: Strategic overview: courses of action, capabilities, value streams and resources.

Capability Map.purpose: Structured overview of the enterprise's capabilities.

Value Stream.purpose: Value streams, the capabilities that enable them and the value they deliver.

Outcome Realization.purpose: How outcomes are produced by capabilities and the core elements behind them.

Resource Map.purpose: Resources and the capabilities and work that use them.

Project.purpose: Work packages, events, deliverables and the people and goals involved.

Migration.purpose: Transition from baseline to target through plateaus and gaps.

Implementation and Migration.purpose: Programmes and projects related to plateaus, gaps and the architecture they change.
